title: Parking lot domain model
idea: The parking lot domain model separates the fixed layout (ParkingLot, Floor, ParkingSpot, gates) from the per-visit records (Vehicle, Ticket, Payment) that change all day.

analogy.text: A building floor plan and the visitor log at reception. The plan stays the same for years; the log gets new lines every hour.
analogy.breaks: A real log accepts any line; a Ticket refuses a misfit.

points: A ParkingLot has Floors and gates; each Floor owns its ParkingSpots.
A Ticket links one Vehicle to one ParkingSpot from entry to exit.
VehicleType lists the SpotTypes it fits, so the fit rule lives once.
A Payment settles one Ticket; FeeStrategy computes its amount in paise.

edges.label: has 1..*
edges.caption: A ParkingLot owns one or more Floors. Floors never move between lots.

edges.label: has 1..*
edges.caption: A Floor owns its ParkingSpots. Each spot has a fixed SpotType.

edges.label: has 1..*
edges.caption: The lot has entry and exit gates. They are thin and hold no rules.

edges.label: for 1
edges.caption: A Ticket is for exactly one Vehicle, identified by its normalised plate.

edges.label: uses 1
edges.caption: A Ticket stores the spot id it was given. The fit rule is checked here.

edges.label: settles 1
edges.caption: A Payment settles one Ticket. Its amount is a long in minor units.

edges.label: prices
edges.caption: FeeStrategy is an interface. The next page plugs in an hourly fee.

code.title: The model in Java 17
code.caption: Records for fixed data; classes for ParkingSpot (behaviour) and Ticket (its status changes). Invariants live in constructors.

walk.text: Build the fixed layout: one floor with three spot types and two gates.
A messy plate is cleaned by Vehicle, then a Ticket puts the car in F1-C1.
A truck in a COMPACT spot is refused by the Ticket constructor.
A negative Payment is refused too.
VehicleType carries its fitting spot types, smallest first.
The compact constructor normalises the plate and rejects a blank one.
Ticket checks the fit rule; status is the only field that changes.

pitfalls: Do not subclass Vehicle per type; a VehicleType enum with fit sets is enough.
Normalise plates in one place, or one car becomes two different vehicles.
Keep fees as long paise; double arithmetic rounds money wrongly.

quiz.q: What is the first line ParkingModel prints?
quiz.why: The Vehicle compact constructor strips spaces and upper-cases the plate. A new Ticket starts ACTIVE.

takeaway: Fixed layout and per-visit records are different classes; keep them apart.

starters: Should ParkingSpot know which Ticket is parked in it?
Why is Vehicle a record but Ticket a class?
